name: Ride
label: Creation Records
lede: Four Oxford art students were signed to Creation within a year of their first gig and were 18 to 20 when they made Nowhere. Six years later the two songwriters wouldn't share a side of a record.

eras.title: A demo, a Christmas party, a deal
eras.text: Andy Bell and Mark Gardener knew each other from Cheney School in Oxford and went to art college in Banbury together. Within about a year of the first rehearsal, Alan McGee had signed them to Creation Records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ride (band) · Uncut: We wanted to make a hell of a racket
years.h: Art college in Banbury puts the four of them in one room
years.p: Bell and Gardener start a foundation course in art and design and meet drummer Laurence 'Loz' Colbert. Bassist Steve Queralt, another Cheney old boy, comes from behind the counter at the local Our Price.
years.xp: The name was picked for the sense of travel, and for the ride cymbal. Bell has said a [[The Smiths|40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27]] show was the thing that made him want a band.

years.cap: Ride on stage at Oxford Town Hall
q: By the end of that gig, we were a band.
years.src: Uncut: We wanted to make a hell of a racket · Wikipedia: Ride (band)
years.h: The first gig is the college Christmas party
years.p: Ride plays its debut for classmates at the end of the autumn term. Queralt said the whole ambition was to headline Oxford's Jericho Tavern and fill it.

years.src: Uncut: We wanted to make a hell of a racket · Wikipedia: Ride (band)
years.h: "It needs to be bassier and it needs to be noisier"
years.p: Queralt's note to the engineer at Union Street Studios, a room under a terraced house, during demos with 'Chelsea Girl' and 'Drive Blind'.
years.xp: An earlier version of the demo tape was made in Queralt's bedroom and hallway. The band went back to Union Street in July.

years.src: Uncut: We wanted to make a hell of a racket · Wikipedia: Ride (band)
years.h: Alan McGee sees three gigs in a row, then signs them
years.p: The tape had reached McGee via DJ [[Gary Crowley|fed7f4aa-855e-4294-8a8b-33191696160a]] after [[Jim Reid|cb527b74-05e3-4926-a711-137214e748ac]] of the Mary Chain took an interest. After Ride supported [[The Soup Dragons|5c42c9cf-5833-41d8-b600-177e70894046]], McGee asked: "C'mon then, will you sign with me?"

eras.title: Teenagers on the charts
eras.text: Three EPs and an album in one year, with Melody Maker calling the album breathtaking. Creation Records had never had a top 75 record until Ride gave it one, and an American major was paying six figures an album.

years.src: Uncut: We wanted to make a hell of a racket · Wikipedia: Ride (band)
years.h: The first EP sells 4,000 copies in three days
years.p: Ride goes in at No. 71, Creation's first top 75 placing. It went on to sell more than 60,000. "It charted against all expectations," Gardener said.

years.src: Uncut: We wanted to make a hell of a racket
years.h: Seymour Stein offers $350,000 an album at Royal Holloway
years.p: After a college gig, the Sire Records boss signs Ride for everywhere but the UK.
years.xp: "I'd formed the band, two months later it was happening. That continued for a couple of years," Bell told Uncut.

years.h: Play goes to No. 32
years.p: The second EP of the year. 'Like a Daydream' would come fourth in John Peel's Festive Fifty.

years.h: Nowhere: four 18-to-20-year-olds and a wave that won't break
years.p: Marc Waterman recorded it and [[Alan Moulder|1b75cdb6-4d61-4ff5-b699-28075b867b4c]] mixed it at Swanyard in London. Warren Bolster's photo of an uncrested wave is the cover.
years.xp:
It reached No. 11. 'Vapour Trail' closes the record with strings, and Melody Maker called the album "breathtaking." The September Fall EP was folded into the CD.

The 2011 anniversary edition came with a lenticular sleeve and a live disc from the Roxy, April 10, 1991.

years.h: Two Ride songs finish third and fourth in Peel's Festive Fifty
years.p: After two John Peel sessions that year, listeners vote 'Dreams Burn Down' to No. 3 and 'Like a Daydream' to No. 4. 'Taste' comes in at 25.

years.h: Today Forever turns the noise down and reaches No. 14
years.p: The fourth EP moves away from the wall of feedback.

years.h: Japanese tickets go in minutes
years.p: The first trip abroad takes in Japan, Australia and France.

eras.title: Eight minutes, then two halves
eras.text: Going Blank Again was the commercial peak of the whole scene the press called shoegaze, a word Bell never liked. Two years later the songwriters were bringing in finished songs separately, and the third album was literally split down the middle.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ride (band) · Wikipedia: Going Blank Again
years.h: An eight-minute single goes to No. 9
years.p: 'Leave Them All Behind' becomes Ride's biggest hit and reaches No. 20 on the US alternative chart.

years.h: Twenty-five songs recorded, ten kept, No. 5
years.p: Moulder produces Going Blank Again at Chipping Norton and Blackbarn. It closes on 'OX4', over seven minutes long.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ride (band) · Wikipedia: Going Blank Again
years.h: 'Twisterella', named from Billy Liar, stalls at No. 36
years.p: Creation stops promoting the album after it. Then comes a long American tour.
years.xp: "By the time the second album came out we were touring too much. We were tired," Bell said.

years.h: Ride plays Reading, and the tape keeps rolling
years.p: The 1992 set came out a decade later as Live Reading Festival 1992, part of the 2002 reissue wave.

years.h: Two 'Daytripper' weekends with the Charlatans
years.p: Ride and [[The Charlatans|8434409e-baa9-4e12-b4aa-566a91c7d7cf]] co-headline a double bill, a pairing they would bring back thirty years later.

years.h: Gardener's songs on side one, Bell's on side two
years.p: [[John Leckie|7388621b-7649-40e0-a98b-67ef14938d9d]] produces, a young [[Nigel Godrich|52de022d-5401-427f-8301-ff1b8be11a7a]] engineers, and Deep Purple's Jon Lord plays keys. It goes to No. 5.
years.xp:
Gardener wouldn't let Bell's songs be mixed in among his, and the running order shows it. Instead of jamming songs into shape, both arrived with finished ones.

By the end of the year the band had a nickname for the record: "Carnival of Shite." Bell's verdict: "When we recorded the Carnival of Light album we got indulgent."

eras.title: Crashing the car
eras.text: The fight over Tarantula was about direction: Gardener heard dance music in the band's future and Bell didn't. Gardener left in the middle of the mix, and Creation pulled the record a week after it came out.

years.h: Gardener walks out while Tarantula is being mixed
years.p: Gardener wanted to bring in dance music; Bell disagreed. Bell wrote most of the songs and Gardener one, and Bell's 'Castle on the Hill' is about Gardener's absence.
years.xp: Queralt saw two roads ahead of the band and said they "chose the wrong option."

years.h: Melody Maker makes 'Black Nite Crash' its single of the week
years.p: It reaches No. 67, the last Ride single for 21 years.

years.h: Ride splits, and Creation deletes Tarantula after a week
years.p: Gardener, looking back in 2015. The breakup was announced just before the album came out; it got to No. 21 and was gone from the shops a week later.
years.xp:
"We weren't very good at saying 'no' or 'stop', which might have done us some good," Gardener told NME.

AllMusic was brutal about the album; Rolling Stone said it "rocks harder than anything else Ride have recorded."

eras.title: Hurricane, Oasis, Animalhouse
eras.text: Bell went furthest, ending up in Oasis. Gardener and Colbert started over together, and the four of them met up again once on camera.

years.h: Bell's Hurricane No. 1 stays on Creation
years.p: With singer Alex Lowe, Hurricane No. 1 gets a No. 19 hit with a remix of 'Step into My World'.

years.h: Andy Bell joins Oasis and has to learn the bass
years.p: He replaces Paul McGuigan and learns the instrument and the whole catalogue before his first show. He plays on three Oasis albums.
years.xp: He'd turned down [[Gay Dad|c2cd7d06-4236-470b-badf-f3a52a3992c4]] first. After Oasis split in 2009, Bell moved to guitar in [[Beady Eye|a0e10984-0eca-4920-a171-5fd7a62ee069]].

years.h: All four jam for half an hour on Channel 4
years.p: Filmed for a documentary, the improvisation becomes the 2002 release Coming Up for Air. Gardener and Colbert's band Animalhouse, a hit in Japan, broke up the same year.

eras.title: Back from nowhere
eras.text: The reunion was meant to be a tour. It turned into three more albums on Wichita, two of them produced by Erol Alkan, and a run of nights playing the first two records start to finish.

years.cap: Ride at the 9:30 Club, Washington, DC
years.h: A Primavera banner in Barcelona gives the reunion away
years.p: The festival's tweet of the poster comes first; dates for Europe and North America follow.

years.cap: Ride at Saint Andrews Hall, Detroit, 2015
years.h: Easter Sunday at the old Zodiac, 500 people, first show in 20 years
years.p: Ride warms up in Oxford in the venue where they started out, then flies to Coachella. DIIV open the summer US dates.
years.xp: Before the show they spent time at a house in the countryside. "We just wanted to make sure that there was something there to reunite," Bell said.

years.h: Weather Diaries, the first album in 21 years
years.p: Produced by Erol Alkan, out on Wichita, No. 11. 'Charm Assault' was the first new song since 1996.

years.h: This Is Not a Safe Place reaches No. 7
years.p: Alkan again. It's the band's highest-charting record since 1994.
play: This Is Not a Safe Place

years.cap: Ride at Primavera Sound, Barcelona, June 2022
years.h: Nowhere at 30, played front to back
years.p: At Primavera Sound they play Going Blank Again and Nowhere in full on separate days. In North America the Charlatans join for the co-headlining 'Between Nowhere' tour.

years.h: Interplay goes to No. 8
years.p: The seventh album, led by 'Peace Sign'.

years.cap: Andy Bell with Oasis at the Principality Stadium, Cardiff, July 2025
years.h: Bell is back in Oasis for the reunion tour
years.p: He plays the Oasis Live '25 dates, with Ride still a going concern.

Uncut: It wasn't rock'n'roll, it was much more than that
